questions.question: Maya draws a closed shape with exactly 4 straight sides. Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, all 4 angles are right angles, the two long sides are each 8 cm and the two short sides are each 3 cm. Which name fits this shape best?
options: Rectangle
Square
Rhombus
Trapezoid
questions.explain: Four right angles plus two pairs of parallel sides makes a rectangle. The trap is thinking any shape with 4 right angles must be a square — a square also needs all 4 sides equal, and here the sides are 8 cm and 3 cm.

questions.question: A paper tile has exactly 4 straight sides. Every side measures 5 cm and all 4 angles are right angles. Which statement about this tile is true?
options: It is a square, so it cannot be a rectangle.
It is a square, and it is also a rectangle.
It is a rectangle only if two of its sides are longer than the other two.
It is not a quadrilateral, because all 4 of its sides are equal.
questions.explain: A rectangle is any 4-sided shape with 4 right angles, so a square is a special rectangle that also has all 4 sides equal. The common trap is thinking a rectangle must have two long sides and two short sides.

questions.question: A closed shape has exactly 4 straight sides. Exactly 1 pair of opposite sides is parallel; the other 2 sides are not parallel to each other. Which name fits this shape?
options: Parallelogram
Rectangle
Trapezoid
Rhombus
questions.explain: Count the pairs of parallel sides: exactly one pair means a trapezoid. A parallelogram, rectangle and rhombus all need two pairs of parallel sides, so one pair is not enough for those names.

questions.question: A closed shape has exactly 4 straight sides. Each side measures 7 cm, there are 2 pairs of parallel sides, and not one of its 4 angles is a right angle. Which name fits this shape?
options: Square
Trapezoid
Rectangle
Rhombus
questions.explain: Four equal sides with two pairs of parallel sides is a rhombus. The trap is thinking 4 equal sides automatically means a square — a square also needs all 4 angles to be right angles, and this shape has none.

questions.question: Ms. Wong puts a hoop on the floor labelled ‘Rectangles’. Which shape does NOT belong inside that hoop?
options: A shape with 4 sides of 5 cm and angles of 60 degrees, 120 degrees, 60 degrees, 120 degrees
A card 12 cm by 8 cm with 2 pairs of parallel sides and 4 right angles
A tile with 4 sides, every side 4 cm, and 4 right angles
A door-shaped piece of wood with 2 pairs of parallel sides and 4 right angles
questions.explain: To be a rectangle a shape needs 4 right angles, so the shape with 60 degree and 120 degree angles is a rhombus and stays out. Watch the trap: the 4 cm tile is a square, and squares do belong in the rectangle hoop.

questions.question: Which statement about quadrilaterals is ALWAYS true?
options: Every rectangle is a square.
Every square is a rectangle.
A square is not a rectangle, because a rectangle needs 2 long sides and 2 short sides.
Every trapezoid is a parallelogram.
questions.explain: A square has 4 right angles and 2 pairs of parallel sides, which is exactly the rule for a rectangle, so every square is a rectangle. Going the other way fails: a 12 cm by 5 cm rectangle is not a square.

questions.question: Leo measures a wooden sign at the ferry terminal. It has 4 straight sides. The top side is 40 cm and the bottom side is 60 cm, and those two sides are parallel. The left and right sides are both 30 cm, but they are not parallel to each other. Which name fits the sign?
options: Rectangle
Parallelogram
Trapezoid
Rhombus
questions.explain: Only one pair of sides is parallel, so the sign is a trapezoid. The trap is using the two equal 30 cm sides to call it a rhombus or parallelogram — equal sides do not make sides parallel.

questions.question: Ana has cut out a 4-sided shape and wants to be sure it is a parallelogram, not just any quadrilateral. Which check should she do?
options: Check that the shape has 4 straight sides.
Check that all 4 sides are the same length.
Check that at least one angle is a right angle.
Check that both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
questions.explain: A parallelogram is defined by having both pairs of opposite sides parallel, so that is the check to make. Equal sides or a right angle can happen in other quadrilaterals too, so those tests do not settle it.

questions.question: In class, Jasmine says a square cannot go in the ‘rectangles’ group because rectangles need a long side and a short side. Nina says the square does belong there. Who is right, and why?
options: Nina is right: a square has 4 right angles and 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is a rectangle with equal sides.
Jasmine is right: a square is a rhombus because all 4 sides are equal, so it cannot also count as a rectangle.
Both are wrong: a square belongs only in the rhombus group, because all its sides are equal, which rectangles never have.
Jasmine is right: a rectangle must have 2 long sides and 2 short sides, and a square's 4 equal sides fail that test.
questions.explain: The rule for a rectangle is 4 right angles and 2 pairs of parallel sides — nothing says the sides must be different lengths, so every square passes the test. A shape can sit in more than one group at once: a square is a rectangle AND a rhombus.

questions.question: A Grade 5 class cuts out 12 paper shapes. Exactly 5 of them have 4 right angles and both pairs of opposite sides parallel; of those 5, exactly 2 also have all 4 sides the same length. The other 7 shapes have no right angles at all. How many of the 12 shapes are rectangles?
questions.explain: All 5 shapes with 4 right angles and 2 pairs of parallel sides are rectangles, and the 2 with equal sides are squares, which are still rectangles. The trap is subtracting those 2 squares and answering 3.

questions.question: Ben tells his group that any quadrilateral with 4 equal sides must be a square. Deepa then cuts out a shape with 4 sides that each measure 6 cm, with angles of 70 degrees, 110 degrees, 70 degrees and 110 degrees. What does Deepa’s shape show?
options: Ben is right: with 4 sides of 6 cm the shape has to be a square, because equal sides are all a square needs.
The shape is a trapezoid, because its angles are not all the same, and a rhombus needs 4 matching angles.
Ben is wrong: the shape is a rhombus, because equal sides are not enough — a square also needs 4 right angles.
The shape is not a quadrilateral, because none of its angles is a right angle, and quadrilaterals need square corners.
questions.explain: Sorting quadrilaterals needs sides AND angles: 4 equal sides gives a rhombus, and only 4 right angles as well would make it a square. Any closed shape with 4 straight sides is still a quadrilateral, whatever its angles measure.

questions.question: Two hoops overlap on the gym floor. The left hoop is labelled ‘All 4 sides equal’ and the right hoop is labelled ‘All 4 angles are right angles’. Which shape goes in the overlapping part, where both labels are true?
options: A rectangle that is 10 cm by 4 cm
No shape can go there, because a shape cannot be a square and a rectangle at the same time
A shape with 4 sides of 9 cm and angles of 45 degrees and 135 degrees
A shape with 4 sides of 9 cm and 4 right angles
questions.explain: The overlap needs both labels true at once, and 4 sides of 9 cm with 4 right angles is a square, which fits both. Remember that one shape can wear two names, so a square really is a rectangle with equal sides.
